added_failures_note: the reviewed run's own manifest names its single gate under test_logs and names no baseline_suite/after_suite field, so annotate_review_of_run reads its own count as unmeasured; this count is derived from the two arms the review ran itself at the reviewed run's own base and head revisions - logs/gate-base-arm.log (revision 84b6364f, module /tmp/review-arms-stored-head/base/reckon/crew/recovery.py, 9 passed, EXIT=0) and logs/gate-head-arm.log (revision a8422de3, module /tmp/review-arms-stored-head/head/reckon/crew/recovery.py, 10 passed, EXIT=0). Neither arm failed, so no failing node id was added; the head arm's tenth case is the one the change adds, and it passes.
call_sites: the changed function is private to reckon/crew/recovery.py and has three production callers there: dispatch_review_for_run (recovery.py:1365)

findings.text: - _stored_review passes head=_run_head_for_review(record) but tree=_review_tree(record); once the worktree is gone the tree is the shared checkout, so a record that names no revision is reconstructed by review_described_head and _revision_at against the repository's history rather than the run's worktree, and the two sources can disagree; only records predating the revision field are affected, since a record naming a revision answers directly.

- a reclaimed worktree whose record names neither a manifest commit nor a head makes _record_carried_head return the empty string, and select_review_for_head then takes its 'if not head: return newest' branch (recovery.py:316), accepting the newest stored record for the run whatever revision it describes; the base code resolved a non-empty repository head here, so this edge is newly permissive, and the new case does not cover it. The scenario was not constructed, so this is reported as plausible rather than confirmed.

item_verdicts.diff: read at the revision; the one-line swap is the whole production change, and head carries _run_head_for_review at recovery.py:435, :576 and :1188 where base had it at :435 and :1188, so the classifier now agrees with the dispatch composer and the dropped-lane comparison on which head a review is evidence about.
item_verdicts.done_when: tests/test_rereview_keeps_its_lane.py:386 adds one case over a removed worktree whose record carries the earlier head: a review stored at the repository head is asserted not standing and one stored at the recorded head is asserted standing; both arms reproduce here and the case discriminates — the focused file passes 9 at base 84b6364f and 10 at head a8422de3, and running the head test file against the base module reds the first assertion (1 failed).
item_verdicts.goal: the dispatched goal was to make reckon.crew.recovery._stored_review resolve the reviewed run's current head from the head its run record carries rather than through a reclaimed worktree's fallback to the main checkout; recovery.py:576 swaps one call, from _reviewed_run_head(record) to _run_head_for_review(record), and _run_head_for_review (recovery.py:1100) already returns _reviewed_run_head while the worktree is readable and _record_carried_head once it is gone, so the surface the goal names is exactly the change and nothing else moves.
item_verdicts.manifest: its commits, changed_paths, tests and negative_control_log match the tree; logs/gate-rereview-lane.log reads 10 passed EXIT=0 and logs/negative-control-red.log repeats the declared mutation verbatim and ends 1 failed EXIT=1; it names its arms under tests/test_logs rather than under baseline_suite/after_suite, so the crew reader's own added-failure derivation reads unmeasured against this manifest.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the grant is recovery.py, the test file, an evidence fragment and a figures directory; commit a8422de3 touches exactly reckon/crew/recovery.py (1 insertion, 1 deletion) and tests/test_rereview_keeps_its_lane.py (53 insertions, 0 deletions), and the fragment and figures paths are correctly left unused because the done-when names no artifact; no plan edit and no terminal status.

justifications.durability: a regression that restores _reviewed_run_head reds the new case, which I demonstrated against the base module, and the case asserts both halves so a one-sided fix cannot pass it, and it uses the isolated_project fixture and touches no real store; deducted because two paths the change leaves open are uncovered: a legacy record naming no revision is still reconstructed through _review_tree, and a reclaimed worktree whose record names neither a manifest commit nor a head resolves to an empty head that selects the newest record regardless of revision.
justifications.evidence: both arms reproduced here to the node's own counts (base 9 passed, head 10 passed, EXIT=0 both) and I reddened the defect independently by running the head test file against the base module (1 failed on the first assertion), so the case discriminates; deducted because the reviewed gate log's own revision line names 84b6364f plus an uncommitted change rather than the delivered commit a8422de3, tying the passing gate to the commit only by the node's word until re-run, and because the manifest's arm evidence sits under test_logs rather than baseline_suite/after_suite.
justifications.fit: the change reuses _run_head_for_review, the helper the composed dispatch (recovery.py:435) and the dropped-lane comparison (recovery.py:1188) already read, rather than adding a second head-resolution path; no new symbol and no plan identifier; deducted because _stored_review still pairs that recorded head with tree=_review_tree(record), which for a reclaimed worktree is the shared checkout, so the head and the tree a legacy record is reconstructed from come from two different sources.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the swap is exactly the stated goal and the helper it now calls already carries the recorded-head semantics, so only the reclaimed-worktree case changes: a live worktree still resolves through _reviewed_run_head and a record naming no worktree still falls back to its repository, both unchanged from base, and all three callers key on the same head afterwards.
justifications.scope_discipline: two changed paths, both inside the grant; the granted evidence fragment and figures directory are correctly unused because the done-when names no artifact; the commit carries a conventional subject and a body, no plan or sprint identifier appears in the change, and no plan state, index or peer path is touched.
